text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

And that was when a door opened down the hallway behind her, releasing two voices into the room. One female, one male; one asking a question, the other replying; neither loud nor excited, just casual conversation. Jonah released her hand and turned away to look down the hall at them.
When Mara heard the voices and followed his gaze, she saw one young man who wasn’t Jonah, but close in size and shape; he had brown hair and a beard and was carrying a glass.

The brown-haired man glanced once over his shoulder, saw them standing there, nodded hello, and stepped right into the gathering, holding up his glass of wine—a half-full plastic cup with the Fulcrum logo on it. “Cheers.” He set it on the table against the wall to the left of the door, and stepped forward to shake Jonah’s hand as they exchanged names.

As he set down the glass and moved out of its space, a previously unseen catering worker entered from the hallway behind him and retrieved it. She wore the same black-and-white striped Fulcrum uniform shirt, though she looked old enough to have had that job since the Institute was founded; and she gave no outward sign of the social fact that she was taking their discarded drink back to the kitchen, while the rest of the conversation went on.

Mara watched this woman return to the hallway where she belonged, and noticed herself noticing who assumed whose labor.

segment:
Adrian’s voice joined the conversation then, arriving in the space with him a moment later.  “Do you see anyone we’ve missed?” he asked.
“Everyone’s here,” said the other man. “No one has left yet.”
Adrian didn’t contradict the second man, though Mara had noticed his late arrival and no one had left their original seats since she arrived. “And what about the glass?” Adrian asked instead of disagreeing, as he sat down. He gestured to the spot on the table where the half-empty cup of red wine had just stood for a few moments; the brown-haired man had finished his first sip and set it aside as if done with the drink.

Jonah followed Adrian’s gaze and then Mara did, too. “No glass here,” she said aloud.
“It’s already gone,” Jonah agreed, then glanced over at her. She was sitting on a nearby couch, still watching Adrian as he studied the space where the wineglass had been.

“I want everyone to see what I see,” Adrian explained, and turned to face the room again. His voice remained perfectly steady in an ordinary volume; no one needed to lean in to hear him over the air-conditioner. “That glass contained a half-full cup of wine. And now it’s gone.”
“What’s wrong with that?” the brown-haired man asked. “The waiter took it away.”
Jonah snorted in agreement. The man who had spoken seemed to realize he might be taking sides too early in this dispute, but by then Adrian was looking at him already, and asked a question instead of disagreeing.

“Do you still remember where it was?”

segment:
1. As they talk, Mara sees a man enter through another door and stride into the center of the gathering: Adrian, introduced by name. 
2. After being introduced in turn, Mara looks up from one interaction and sees Jonah watching her instead. (He doesn't talk to her directly. He is also not flirting, just studying her.) 
3. She turns back to Adrian, who comments that someone must have been talking about him. He asks who it was.
4. Mara gestures to the glass and the catering worker, saying that she watched that. Adrian asks how he might know this if he weren't here.
5. She tells Adrian a general version, without names; he says that's not close enough. 
6. She names Jonah. Adrian asks her to keep going until she tells everything she saw in detail, not what she was thinking.
7. When she says that Jonah seemed to have watched her for a long moment when she first entered the room, Adrian points out that she didn't know that then. Mara insists that Jonah did it before their conversation even began. Adrian asks why she's bringing this up at all.
8. Mara asks if he really wants her to tell him how Jonah was looking at her. He does; she asks him not to be offended. 
9. Mara tells the interaction again, making it clear that she saw Jonah watching her as soon as she entered the room. She says it seemed to last the length of her exhale, though it could've been shorter.
